title: Voice Agent Red-Teaming and Jailbreak Testing
summary: Adversarial phone calls against your voice agent in Hindi, Hinglish and English, testing verification bypass, data leakage, prompt injection and off-script promises, with recorded evidence.

seo.title: Voice Agent Red-Teaming and Jailbreak Testing | VipraTech
seo.description: Adversarial calls in Hindi, Hinglish and English that test voice agents for verification bypass, data leakage and prompt injection, with audio evidence.

problem.intro: A voice agent connected to account systems is a new front door for fraud. Callers can try to talk it past verification, coax out another customer's details, trigger a SIM replacement request or get it to promise a waiver it has no authority to give. They can also switch language or talk over it to slip past guardrails that were only tested in English text.

pain_points.title: Text-only testing misses voice paths
pain_points.detail: Barge-in, background voices, DTMF input and speech recognition errors create attack routes that a chat-based test never exercises.

pain_points.title: Social engineering and SIM fraud
pain_points.detail: Impersonation and urgency tactics that work on human agents can work on voice agents too, with direct fraud consequences.

pain_points.title: Language switching evades guardrails
pain_points.detail: A refusal that holds in English can fail when the same request is made in Hinglish or a regional language.

pain_points.title: No repeatable evidence
pain_points.detail: Ad hoc testing before launch leaves nothing to re-run when the prompt, model or tools change.

solution.overview: We test your voice agent the way a determined caller would, over the same phone line or SIP endpoint your customers use. We build multi-turn attack playbooks for your agent's scope: verification bypass and impersonation, account and personal data leakage, prompt injection through spoken instructions, system prompt disclosure, unauthorised actions such as SIM replacement or plan changes, off-script offers and refunds, and abusive responses. Synthetic caller voices run the playbooks in Hindi, Hinglish, English and agreed regional languages, with accents, background noise, interruptions and DTMF input. Every call is recorded, scored PASS, RISK or FAIL and verified by an engineer, and you keep a regression suite to re-run after changes.
capabilities: Attack playbooks for verification bypass, impersonation, data leakage, prompt injection and unauthorised actions
Calls over real telephony or SIP with synthetic voices, accents, noise, barge-in and DTMF
Language-switching attacks across Hindi, Hinglish, English and agreed regional languages
PASS, RISK and FAIL scoring with call audio, transcript and the turn where the failure occurred
Findings mapped to OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications and MITRE ATLAS techniques
Re-runnable regression suite for testing after prompt, model or tool changes

workflow.title: Agree scope and rules
workflow.detail: Test numbers, synthetic accounts, call windows and in-scope behaviours are agreed in writing.

workflow.title: Build attack playbooks
workflow.detail: Multi-turn playbooks are tailored to the agent's intents, tools, languages and fraud risks.

workflow.title: Place adversarial calls
workflow.detail: Synthetic callers run the playbooks over SIP or phone lines, with noise, interruptions and DTMF.

workflow.title: Score and verify
workflow.detail: Each call is scored PASS, RISK or FAIL, and an engineer listens to every ambiguous or failing call.

workflow.title: Report findings
workflow.detail: Findings with audio, transcripts, framework mapping and fix suggestions go to your product and security teams.

workflow.title: Retest
workflow.detail: After fixes, the same playbooks run as a regression suite to confirm closure.

inputs: Voice agent test number or SIP endpoint
Agent scope, system prompt and tool list where shared
Known fraud patterns and past incidents
human_in_the_loop: Engineers verify every RISK and FAIL call by listening to the audio before it is reported. Your security and product owners decide severity, fixes and go-live readiness.
integrations: SIP trunks and test phone numbers
In-house or vendor voice agent platforms
Jira or similar for findings tracking
guardrails: Tests run only against test numbers and synthetic accounts agreed in writing
No real customer data used or requested
Call rates and windows limited to avoid disrupting operations
Production fraud controls tested only with explicit approval
Evidence encrypted and shared with named contacts only
compliance_notes: Results are mapped to the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications and MITRE ATLAS to help your team evidence testing; they do not certify the agent.
Test evidence can support DPDP Act 2023 expectations for reasonable security safeguards in systems that handle customer data.

pilot.scope: One voice agent and one high-risk flow, such as account information or SIM-related requests, with a fixed playbook set and one retest.
deliverables: Threat model and test plan for the pilot flow
Recorded adversarial calls with verified results
Findings report with audio evidence and fixes
Regression suite for the pilot flow

what_we_measure.how: Playbooks executed per category in the agreed test plan.
RISK and FAIL results confirmed by engineer review of the audio.
Findings that recur when the same playbook is re-run before fixes.
Findings closed on retest after the client team's changes.

faqs.q: Will testing affect our production systems or customers?
faqs.a: We test against test numbers and synthetic accounts agreed in writing, in agreed time windows and at controlled call rates. If you want production testing, it is scoped separately with your security and operations teams.

faqs.q: Which voice platforms can you test?
faqs.a: Any agent reachable by a phone number or SIP endpoint, whether built in-house or on a vendor platform. For agents with tool access, we also review the tool permissions and test them through the conversation.

faqs.q: Do you test in regional languages?
faqs.a: Yes. Hindi, Hinglish and English are standard, and regional languages are added where your agent supports them, because a guardrail that holds in one language can fail in another.
After every change to the model, prompt, tools or knowledge base, and on a regular schedule otherwise. The regression suite we hand over can run from your CI pipeline or on demand.
